subject: Private deployment: CMK responsibilities, operator access slices, and handoff cadence
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@arcadialabs.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.p@arcadialabs.com>, procurement@arcadialabs.com
Date: Sun, 16 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment queries: CMK split and operator "slices"

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week — Arcadia's security and procurement teams had a few follow-ups while we review the private deployment (VPC) option. We've attached our initial DPA redlines (arcadia_dpa_redlines_v1.pdf). High level asks: 

- Can Redwood confirm the exact operator responsibilities when the customer supplies the CMK (BYOK)? Specifically: who can rotate/trigger key refresh, who can export the key (if any), and whether there is any scenario where Redwood personnel can access plaintext model I/O?
- We want an "access slices" model: minimal operator visibility to metadata only, operator runbooks for breakglass, and a monthly attestation that no operator access occurred. Is that feasible?
- Escrow/escrow-release timeline: procurement prefers a documented cadence for handing over keys to an escrow provider if a contractual exit is triggered.

Can you point us to a concise operator-access matrix and suggest language for the DPA where Redwood accepts no access to plaintext under normal operations?

Appreciate a short call if needed.

— Liam
Security Lead, Arcadia Labs
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@arcadialabs.com>
Cc: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.p@arcadialabs.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, procurement@arcadialabs.com
Date: Sun, 16 May 2026 12:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment queries: CMK split and operator "slices"

Liam — thanks for the clear set of asks and the redlines. Quick summary while we pull attachments and a short operator matrix together:

1) BYOK responsibilities: when the customer supplies the CMK, Arcadia retains exclusive control over key material. Redwood will require a customer-managed KMS role to unwrap and mount keys for the runtime; we do not persist key material in our control plane. Operationally: Redwood engineers can request ephemeral session tokens that allow limited runtime access (no export of raw key material).

2) Operator visibility: we can support an "access slices" model where operator tooling surfaces only anonymized control-plane telemetry (task IDs, resource metrics, request counts) and not the raw model I/O. We already ship a minimal operator telemetry profile for Private that excludes payloads by default.

3) Breakglass & attestation: we can propose a contractual monthly attestation that states no operator read access to plaintext occurred, and define an emergency breakglass procedure requiring multi‑party signoff (customer security, Redwood security, and the PM on call). Breakglass audits will be logged and sample artifacts delivered.

4) Escrow cadence: we can provide an escrow timeline doc (escrow-timeline-proposal.docx) with stages: notice, verification window (7 business days), handoff to named escrow provider. We recommend an escrow provider approval process during onboarding.

I'll loop Karthik for the operator-access matrix and Neha for DPA suggested language. If you're open, we can schedule a 30-minute alignment call Wed 18th.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Private deployment queries: CMK split and operator "slices"

Liam / team — adding the technical detail Kaisa asked for in the call:

- Key handling: For Private (VPC/on‑prem) when BYOK is in use, the CMK never leaves the customer KMS. Redwood runs a runtime shim that requests ephemeral key‑usage tokens (via customer-provided KMS role) to decrypt model segments and KV cache in memory. These tokens are short lived (< 15 minutes) and are scoped to the runtime instance.

- No export guarantee: Redwood engineers do not have an admin operation that exports plaintext inputs/outputs from the running process. For additional contractual assurance we can add a non-export clause to the DPA: "Redwood personnel are prohibited from exporting plaintext model I/O except under the defined breakglass procedure."

- Operator slices/masking: we propose three slices: (1) Control (deployment/job state, resource metrics), (2) Observability (aggregated token counts, latency histograms — always aggregated), (3) Emergency (breakglass event, full trace capture). By default #3 is disabled; enabling requires documented and auditable approval steps.

- Auditing & attestation: the runtime will produce an immutable audit bundle for any breakglass event (who, when, approval emails, affected instance IDs). For monthly attestation we can produce an automated signed statement that no breakglass events occurred during the period; if any occurred we'll deliver the audit bundle and a post‑mortem within 5 business days.

Attached is a quick operator_access_matrix_v2.xlsx (matrix rows: action, who can trigger, required approvals, logged artifacts). Happy to walk through the matrix on Wed.

— Karthik

Subject: Re: Private deployment queries: CMK split and operator "slices"

Thanks Liam — this is helpful. A few DPA drafting suggestions inline to make things concrete for your legal team (we've attached a draft clause set in the drive link):

- Non‑access clause: "Redwood will not access, copy, or export customer plaintext model inputs or outputs in Private deployments where the customer supplies and controls the CMK, except under a documented breakglass procedure requiring customer security approval and dual Redwood signoff."

- Breakglass controls: define required signoffs (customer security, Redwood security lead, and on‑call engineering manager). List the artifacts that must be produced within 5 business days.

- Escrow: propose an escrow window of 7 business days post‑notice with a verification checklist (identity proofing, signed attestations). Redwood will hold zero custody of CMK material during this process; escrow is between customer and escrow vendor.

Next steps we propose:
1) Marissa to share a 30‑minute slot Wed 18th 10:00–10:30 PT for alignment (calendar invite sent).
2) Arcadia legal to review the short clause language (we'll post in the Drive folder) and propose any redline edits.
3) Redwood to share the finalized operator_access_matrix and a one‑page attestation template.

If Arcadia can confirm the slot, we'll convert the agreement language into a DPA appendix and append an exhibit listing the approved escrow vendor(s).

Best regards,
Neha Kapoor
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Security, Redwood Inference
